subject: computer-organization-and-architecture

chosen.title: Chapter 10 - Principles of Pipelining, in Basic Computer Architecture
chosen.channel: IIT Delhi, Prof. Smruti R. Sarangi (book distributed free under CC BY-ND)
covers: the pipeline idea, the five stages and the space-time diagram
pipeline registers and the cycle time
the performance equation and the stall model
branch prediction, multiple issue and out-of-order execution
chosen.why: the only source read this run that carries the whole topic, from the definition to the CPI equation, in one voice and with worked numbers; every card's core claim rests on it

chosen.title: Instruction Pipelining (romanised Hindi lesson)
covers: the stage list and the diagram reading rule
the (k + n - 1) timing, speed-up, throughput and efficiency formulas
chosen.why: the only readable non-English source, and the only one that states the speed-up, throughput and efficiency formulas together as an exam sheet with a worked numerical; its three 'common mistakes' are the basis of three trap fields

chosen.title: Pipeline Hazards & Stalls (romanised Hindi lesson)
covers: the three hazard classes with a remedy each
the RAW, WAR and WAW table
the control-hazard penalty and the prediction strategies
chosen.why: it is the only source read this run that states the three stall counts together (2 without forwarding, 0 with EX forwarding, 1 for load-use) and the only one that lists the prediction strategies by name

chosen.title: NOC Computer Organization and Architecture: A Pedagogical Aspect - Module 6, Performance Enhancement of Processor
covers: the teaching order: module 5 is peripherals and I/O, module 6 is performance enhancement of the processor
chosen.why: read only to confirm that pipelining follows the I/O interface in the sequence the previous run finished; no sentence of any lecture rests on it and no card quotes it

rejected.why: the digimat PDF transcripts of the Guwahati course answered HTTP 403 to every request from the sandbox, through the egress proxy, and the two module-6 lecture numbers tried (lec39, lec40) returned an empty body to the fetch service, so nothing could be read from the lecture that teaches this topic in the same course whose lectures 33 to 35 supplied the previous run

the IIT Kharagpur 'Computer Architecture and Organization' series has exactly the right lectures - 40 Basic Pipelining Concepts, 41 Pipeline Scheduling, 55 to 58 Pipeline Hazards - and its lecture index was read, but the digimat lecture page for L40 served a title and no transcript, and the transcript PDF path returned an empty body, so it is recorded as structure only and no card draws on it

every YouTube watch page tried answered LOGIN_REQUIRED with no caption track, so no English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu or Bengali lecture supplied a single sentence; this includes the GO Classes and Gate Smashers pipelining lectures and the NPTEL Lec 7 'Instruction Pipeline Hazards' video
both hosts answered 502 through the egress proxy on every attempt, so neither could be read

the standard reference for this topic, but no copy was fetched this run and none of its text is reproduced; the topic rests on a freely distributed IIT Delhi chapter instead, and the disagreement that matters (the exact number of load-use stalls) is checked against computation rather than against a book I could not open

used to locate questions and to corroborate answers, never as the source of a card; their year and question numbering disagree with each other and with the printed papers (2026 Set 1 Q.16 is Q.6 on GATE Overflow, 2025 Set 2 Q.56 is Q.46, 2024 Set 1 Q.30 is Q.20, 2024 Set 2 Q.31 is Q.21 and Q.58 is Q.48, 2022 Q.61 is Q.51, 2020 Q.43 is Q.53 on one index, 2015 Set 3 Q.47 is Q.39 in the paper), and every such disagreement is recorded in the PYQ record rather than resolved

standard_refs: Sarangi, Basic Computer Architecture, chapter 10 (IIT Delhi, free PDF), sections 10.1-10.11
Patterson and Hennessy, Computer Organization and Design, chapter 4 - cited as the standard treatment, not fetched
